title: Add throughput status section and throughput review to Athena
summary: Athena status gains a throughput section computed from job records (landed per day, median minutes per landed job by stage, idle time, time on failed jobs). A throughput review runs every 10 landings or on a >20% worsening, asks a strong model for the biggest bottleneck and architectural fix, queues one design request via the shared steward request builder, and later records predicted vs measured minutes. Audience: Sri and the maintainers who want Athena to find its own speedups.

defaults_applied.how: Tests, fmt and clippy -D warnings are criteria.
Behavior criteria run named cargo test commands.
Design doc and changelog written for outside readers.
Criteria assert measured numbers and queued requests, not wiring.
Review cadence is enforced by code triggers, tested.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (error_review, review_passes, root_cause_request, repeated_causes; review_passes is the entry point running reviews after a landing, and the new throughput review is added there beside the error review and code-health passes), crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (status rendering), crates/athena-core/src/code_health.rs (design-review cadence of 10 landings, reused for the counter), and crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (AnyRecord at line ~2386 and check_record_file at ~2686 are the records validation that accepts a new record kind by path and schema).
Throughput is computed directly from existing job records (timestamps per stage, outcomes), not a stand-in; stage durations come from the same records status already reads.

The prediction record (bottleneck, change, expected minutes saved, cited request, later measured minutes) reuses an existing record type if one fits; if a new record kind is added to crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, it gets a path, schema tag, an AnyRecord variant, check_record_file acceptance and a round-trip test in that file modelled on a_hestia_sweep_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips. This is why records.rs is listed at moderate probability.

The design request goes through the existing shared steward request builder used by root_cause_request; priority maps from expected minutes saved (more minutes, higher priority). Duplicate suppression looks for an open request from a prior throughput review.
Model calls in tests use the existing fake-model facility; no real model is called.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml) do not change; the 'strong model' uses an existing configured model setting, and no cadence constant needs a config entry.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`: a test with fixture job records asserts status output reports landed jobs per day, median minutes per landed job with per-stage values (reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier, landing and rebuild), idle time between jobs, and time spent on non-landed jobs, with exact expected numbers.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: a fake-model test shows a throughput review queues exactly one design request containing the bottleneck, proposed change and predicted minutes saved, and a second review run while it is open queues none.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: a test shows the review triggers at 10 landings since the last review and when median minutes per landed job worsens by more than 20%, and does not trigger otherwise.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: a test shows that after a cited change lands, the next review records predicted against measured minutes per landed job for it.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: a test shows request priority rises with expected minutes saved.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the throughput section and review, and docs/design/hestia.md states the cadence (every 10 landings or >20% worsening) and the prediction-vs-measured follow-up.
Any new record kind is accepted by check_record_file / AnyRecord in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs and has a round-trip test there; if no new kind is added, records.rs is unchanged.

out_of_scope: Changing the error review or code-health review behavior
departures: Larger than reference: multi-file change with a new review, status computation and several tests.
urgent_reason: Targets the biggest pipeline waits (idle time, failed-job time), cutting wasted time per landed job.
hard_reason: Adds a review that triggers on landings and queues work requests (pipeline-shaping automation that can hold or add queue items), so mistakes are costly.
